mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns. At the current level of 5.26% (below the 10-year historical average of 5.5%), the model predicts positive returns due to reduced discount rates for equity valuation.
evidence_refs: fact:10-year historical average of FEDFUNDS is 5.5%
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS level and 20d returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 0.3 percentage points over three months signals an impending recession, prompting monetary policy easing which boosts equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between UNRATE rise >0.3pp in 3 months and positive 20d returns
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE rises >0.3pp in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) both rise above their 3-month moving averages, it indicates a robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both above their 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: The interaction of INDPRO and HOUST both above their 3-month moving averages fails to produce positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (defined by GDP growth above 3% and unemployment below 4.5%), a higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:late-cycle expansion defined by GDPC1 growth >3% and UNRATE <4.5%
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, FEDFUNDS level fails to predict negative returns: 20d returns are positive in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:INDPRO level above 100 indicates strong economy
failure_condition: Rank IC between INDPRO level and 20d returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1500 thousand units, it signals a weak housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:historical correlation between HOUST < 1500 and negative 20d returns
failure_condition: HOUST falls below 1500 fails to produce negative 20d returns: returns are positive in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 204 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is stable (<= 5.26%), it signals that the Fed is not cutting rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction of CPIAUCSL > 204 and FEDFUNDS <= 5.26 fails to produce negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of residential fixed investment (RSAFS) indicates strong housing market activity, which is a leading indicator of economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC between RSAFS level and 60d returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
